models.summary: A stock-conversion account of the forest plus a stock-change account of the products. Carbon density is volume per hectare times an expansion coefficient, a volume coefficient, and a carbon content. Area in year i is the starting area times one minus the cut plus the planting, raised to i. Forest carbon is that area times the density times one plus an understory coefficient and a land coefficient, divided by 1000, and the 1000 sits on the next line. The lagged area feeds an inflow: cut area times a wood-conversion factor times four production ratios over total production, each times a carbon factor. The factors print as 0.225, 0.765, 0.294, and 0.45, under a header that runs the first two product names together. Product carbon is the 2000 stock, given as 10,530 kilotons, decayed by a first-order rate, plus a fraction of this year's inflow. Equation 6 prints the inflow as Infolw. Total carbon is the sum of the two pools. The prose also says the global product stock grows by about 139 hectares a year.
models.computational_cost: A yearly area update and a one-step product decay, swept over cut and planting rates

models.summary: Yang's bat search, with a velocity weight added so the early flight teaches the later one. The weight falls from its maximum toward its minimum by an exponential in the squared fraction of the iteration budget, and that exponent is broken across the line. Frequency is a random point between the bat's minimum and maximum. Velocity is the weighted previous velocity plus loudness times the gap from the best position times the frequency. The printed velocity line has no parentheses around the gap. Position is the best position plus the new velocity, and a step outside the box is projected onto the boundary. Step 4 accepts a new solution when it is greater than itself. Algorithm 1 accepts a step when the new value is less than the current best and a random draw is below the loudness. One test maximizes and the other minimizes. On Russia the search returns a cut of 0.000105 and a planting of 0.003.

models.summary: Twelve indicators in three axes, weighted by entropy, then read as a vector. Logs, forest food, and herbs are priced as quality times a price index times a unit price times a stock. Forest-land value is a present value of logging revenue, a fee, an interest rate, and a period, and equation 13 does not parse. Water value and water purification share one rainfall-minus-evaporation form. Scores are normalized as a benefit, a cost, or a band. Entropy weights print as 0.19, 0.18, 0.18, 0.45 on carbon, summing to 1, with wood products at 0.45. Economy prints 0.47, 0.12, 0.13, 0.26, summing to 0.98. Ecology prints 0.13, 0.20, 0.33, 0.16, summing to 0.82, while the prose points at water purification and water adjustment rather than at the largest weight. The three scores form a vector whose ideal is (1, 1, 1). The plan's score is the length of that vector. Equation 30 lists the axes as carbon, ecology, economy, and the vector is carbon, economy, ecology. On China the 2020 length is 0.9689 and the 2025 length is 0.8716. On Sudan after the plan the three scores are 0.9534, 0.9431, and 0.9583, and the length is 1.648.
